subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom cooperative glob walker and bootstrap-only handler yielding as the bounded fix for this event-loop stall despite possible glob-order and session-timing differences?
rationale: The implementation and proof support the performance fix, but bootstrap files and hooks directly shape prompt bytes and agent state, so automation should not unilaterally accept the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, and land after the exact head passes required checks.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but require one current-head embedded-run or channel-latency transcript demonstrating responsive channel I/O during bootstrap.

options.title: Pause For Broader Architecture
options.body: Hold or close the PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching over this focused mitigation.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, and land after the exact head passes required checks.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest merged-history connection to the bootstrap, guarded-read, and internal-hook boundaries affected by the choice.
